caveats: The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and the independent native-local build-core run reproduced the easyrpg_libretro.zip package, resolver metadata, both ABI artifacts, and both active-marker build logs byte for byte. Execution was local; both builds cloned the pinned source over the network, so no offline source cache is proven.

This is static build/package evidence only. ARM64 is build-identity-bound to ra64-universal-v1 and ARMHF to ra32-a30-v1. ARMHF requires GLIBCXX_3.4.32, above the observed non-enforcing Miyoo Mini fallback provider value GLIBCXX_3.4.24, so the Mini profile is ineligible; A30 is the eligible 32-bit consumer at the ABI screen. Provider inspection and target-runtime capture are absent, so every execution profile and device view remains provisional and ineligible pending a runtime smoke result.

Content, BIOS/firmware handling, controls, audio/video pacing, saves and state round trips, reset and unload behavior, frontend integration, compatibility, licensing review, and sustained performance remain target-runtime and human gates. Publication remains disabled regardless of local byte reproducibility.

The reviewed feature envelope intentionally differs from a desktop build: liblcf is pinned at commit 666e6c02 (tree-asserted at configure time), ICU 78.3 is statically embedded with EasyRPG's trimmed converter-only data set (Shift_JIS/CP932-class encoding detection preserved), audio decoders are limited to the shipped working core's set (Vorbis, mpg123, libsndfile, built-in FmMidi MIDI; no WildMIDI/FluidSynth patchset synths), font rendering is the built-in bitmap font (FreeType off), and LZH archive input is off. Every DT_NEEDED name (libpng16.so.16, libz.so.1, and the loader base set) is present in every probed device capture; the previously shipped arm64 build dynamically linked desktop libraries absent from all devices and could not load.
